picks.why: There's no general admission here. University is one of the cheapest seats and watches the Turn 4 DRS pass.
Covered seats facing the grid, start and podium, right beside the main fan zone and parking.
Outside the heavy Turn 1 braking zone, Bahrain's main overtaking spot.
All-inclusive suites above the team garages, with pit lane walks.
One of F1's cheapest passes, with fan zones and concerts. Trackside views are low and fenced.
Covered and cheaper than Main, with cars passing twice — out of Turn 8 and back through Turns 17–18.
Covered seats at Turns 1–2, the end of the longest DRS zone and Jeddah's prime overtaking spot.
Hospitality above the pits, with pit lane walks and driver appearances.
Some of F1's best GA: grassy mounds and raised platforms, including at Turns 1–2.
On the start-finish straight facing the grid, a short walk from the podium.
Outside Turn 1 at the apex, for the start and most of the race's passing.
Roam the entertainment stages, fan activations and the Turn 1 hill all weekend.
Next to the Kids Area and food; kids 3–14 get about 20% off grandstand seats.
Top-tier hospitality above the pit lane, with paddock access.
Grass banks and unreserved terraces at Spoon Curve and 130R, Suzuka's fastest corners.
Popular Turn 1 stand for the start and plenty of passing.
High seats above the final chicane, the last-lap overtaking spot, with a wide panorama.
Family-only area with stroller parking, changing rooms and cheap child tickets.
Suites above the Suzuka pits with views of the grid, pit stops and podium.
F1's cheapest ticket, on the grass outside the Turn 14 hairpin where most overtakes happen.
Affordable, partly covered hairpin stand, close to the fan zone.
Where the long back straight ends in a heavy stop for Turn 14, with several big screens.
Hospitality above the pits — among the season's lowest Paddock Club prices.
Cheapest entry: roam the campus zones and Hard Rock Stadium seats. Trackside views are limited.
Sweeping view of the start and Turns 1–3; upper rows are covered.
Covers Turns 17–19 at the end of the back straight, Miami's main late-braking pass.
Turns 11–12 beside The Beach, with trackside performances all weekend.
Open bar and a terrace above the team garages.
Cheapest way in. The best GA spot is by the hairpin — arrive early.
Faces the Senna Corner and pit exit with a big screen; often called Montreal's best seat.
Tall stand facing the hairpin's entry and exit, a prime overtaking spot.
The Senna Corner stands are where the party is, plus the uphill run to Turn 3.
Dedicated family stand at Turns 6–7; kids 11 and under get a discount with an adult.
Hospitality above the team garages, with paddock access and the start below.
Hillside general admission above the final corners, with harbour views.
Monaco's biggest stand, over the harbour from Tabac to the Piscine, with a big screen.
At Sainte-Dévote (Turn 1), home of first-lap late braking. No big screen.
The ultimate Monaco hospitality, above the pit lane.
Raised natural hillsides between Turns 11 and 14, with big screens and the fan zones.
The only covered stand, facing the grid and pits, with most of the lap visible from the top.
Outside Turn 1, the heaviest braking point — first-lap scrambles and late-braking passes.
All-inclusive hospitality with track views and behind-the-scenes paddock access.
Head for Vale — a raised bank looking from Stowe's exit towards Club.
Covered and near the podium, with views of Stowe, Vale, Club and down the start straight.
Heavy braking at the end of the Hangar Straight — Silverstone's best overtaking spot.
One of Silverstone's own picks for overtaking and crowd atmosphere.
Covered stand where kids 11 and under get 25% off, with fast cars through Copse.
Suites above the pits with fine dining and pit lane walks.
Hillside views across the circuit, plenty of big screens and the fan zones.
Outside Turn 1 looking down the start straight, with a big screen and the Fan Village nearby.
Faces the Turn 3 hairpin, the Red Bull Ring's main heavy-braking overtaking spot.
The biggest stand, from Turn 1 up to Turn 3, with a dedicated Verstappen fan section.
Kids 14 and under go free with a ticketed adult if booked ahead; two family-friendly fan zones.
Air-conditioned suite above the pits with a roof terrace over the grid.
Roam the whole Ardennes lap — the grassy bank at Pouhon is the best free spot.
Covered, facing the pits and grid: the start, the podium and braking into La Source.
Top of Raidillon, watching cars flat out through Eau Rouge, F1's most famous corner.
At the foot of Raidillon, right in the hub of fan activities.
The promoter's family pick: reserved seats, with discounted children's tickets.
All-inclusive hospitality looking straight onto Eau Rouge and Raidillon.
Grass banks around Turns 9–14 overlook the natural bowl; roam all weekend.
Above the final corner looking down the main straight, a short walk from the fan zone.
Overlooks Turn 1, the Hungaroring's best — almost only — real overtaking spot.
Between Turns 11 and 12, with the fan zone stage right behind it.
The only fully covered stand — shade in Budapest's summer heat, facing the pits and start.
Above the pits with seated dining and daily pit lane walks.
Roam Lesmo, Ascari and Parabolica, then join Monza's famous podium track invasion.
Sees the Ascari chicane and the run to Parabolica, with a big screen opposite.
Closest to the Turn 1 apex — Monza's hardest braking zone and main overtaking spot.
The historic stand opposite the grid, packed with tifosi and facing the podium invasion.
Kids 11 and under get into the lawn areas free with an adult.
Hospitality above the pits at the Temple of Speed, with pit lane access.
Cheapest way in, with standing zones on the main straight, the fast section and the chicane.
On the main straight with the start, pit lane and podium, giant screens and part-covered seats.
Watch cars on La Monumental, F1's longest and steepest banked corner.
Above the pit garages — the top-tier way to see Madrid's new race.
Best of the affordable stands — two straights with cars racing in opposite directions.
Clear views of the Turn 16 exit, right in front of the Fanzone.
Main stand: Section E faces the Turn 1 braking zone, Section C the start and pits.
Inside the Old City, where cars squeeze past castle walls on a 7.6 m-wide track.
Affordable, with the Fanzone right behind; kids 2–16 get about 30% off.
Above the pits on the start/finish straight, with daily pit lane walks.
Cheapest way in — Istanbul Park's hilly layout gives decent views from the GA banks.
F1's top hospitality, with lounges above the team garages on the main straight.
Cheapest ticket — still includes the Padang Stage concerts and Zone 4 viewing spots.
Overlooks the final corners with the skyline and Singapore Flyer behind.
Cars brake hard from about 290 km/h — and the ticket covers all four zones.
Next to the Padang Stage headline concerts, facing the Turn 10 'Singapore Sling'.
Juniors get up to 50% off 3-day seats, near the Empress Lawn family zone.
Chef-led dining and an open bar above the pit lane, with access to every zone.
COTA's hills make great GA — the Turn 1 hillside looks down on the braking zone.
Covers the stadium section and back straight; pick an upper row in sections 2–7.
High above the uphill Turn 1 hairpin — the best seat for the start and first lap.
Two levels of hospitality directly above the pit garages.
The cheapest seat at the circuit, overlooking the long main straight.
In the stadium, facing the podium, with a giant screen and cars coming towards you.
Wide view of the first three corners, where most passes happen.
The Foro Sol stadium — the loudest crowd on the calendar, with the podium and DJ sets.
Pick the Foro Sol level for the stadium buzz, or above the pits for the grid.
Cheapest sector, on the back-straight overtaking spot and closest to the station.
Covered, numbered seats facing the garages, with indoor toilets and a food court.
Covered stand outside the Senna S, where most opening-lap passes happen.
Gourmet hospitality above the pit lane, with driver appearances.
Cheapest way in, with views of the flat-out Koval straight.
Best-value reserved seat at Turn 17, now linked to the Koval and East Harmon zones.
Faces Turn 5 and the Turns 7–9 chicane, with the Sphere lit up behind.
The busiest zone, with the T-Mobile Stage and the Sphere as a backdrop.
Suites above the pit building at the start/finish line, all-inclusive.
A raised bank above Turn 1, the main overtaking spot. Fan Village and concert included.
Numbered seats with some cover, facing the grid, pit lane and podium.
Between the grid and Turn 1, opposite the pit exit — great for the start.
Lively standing crowd above Turn 1, next to the Fan Village and post-race concert.
A balcony above the garages, with gourmet food, an open bar and a track tour.
Cheapest ticket, overlooking Turns 2–6, with the Yasalam concerts included.
Mid-priced reserved seat facing an overtaking spot, with the North Oasis shade nearby.
Faces the heavy braking zone after the 300 km/h back straight, the main passing spot.
A relaxed crowd on the grass, with the Abu Dhabi Hill Oasis fan area nearby.
Kids Go Free: up to four children aged 3–12 get free Friday fan-zone entry.
Above the pit lane, with daily pit lane walks and an all-day open bar.
